_comment: White-label build config for the dotmac_field TECHNICIAN app. Deliberately separate from the repo-root brand.json, which belongs to the customer selfcare app (mobile/): the two are distinct products with distinct store records (io.dotmac.field vs io.dotmac.selfcare) and must be able to diverge without one rebranding the other. Consumed at build time only, via `flutter build --dart-define-from-file=field_mobile/brand.json` — the Android release workflow, the Xcode Cloud post-clone hook, and local `flutter run` all pass this same file. Every key here MUST be read by a String.fromEnvironment in field_mobile/lib (and every BRAND_* key read there MUST appear here); the Field App Release preflight job fails the build on drift in either direction, which is what stops a field build from silently falling back to Flutter's default theme. Values below intentionally mirror the in-code defaults, so introducing this file changes no shipped behaviour. Secrets (SENTRY_DSN) are NEVER stored here - they are injected from CI secrets. Native app identity (applicationId, bundle id, launcher icon/label) is NOT set here; it lives in the android/ and ios/ projects.
_secrets_note: Never add a DSN, key, token or password to this file. It is committed.
_oidc_note: The verified redirect boundary (App Link / Universal Link) the OIDC ceremony comes back through. Fleet-owned and deliberately NOT the API host and NOT a tenant host: the association documents at deploy/links.dotmac.io/ pin ONE application identity, so this origin has to outlive any single deployment or tenant. Changing either value is a five-file change - this file, field_mobile/lib/core/deeplink/oidc_redirect.dart, the Android intent filter, the iOS Associated Domains entitlement, and both association documents - because the OS validates the NATIVE declarations against the documents, not against this string. scripts/check_field_applinks.py fails CI when the five disagree.
